archetype.name: Game Manager (quick-game veteran)
archetype.definition: At nearly 43, Rodgers runs a short, timing-based passing game off the league's best rushing attack, and wins by avoiding damage rather than creating chunk plays.

report.headline: A quick-game caretaker riding the league's best run game, and fading on third down.
report.take:
The Steelers are 6-2 and Rodgers has started all eight, but the record flatters the passer. His -0.095 EPA per dropback ranks 37th of 49 qualifiers, against a league average of -0.002. His CPOE of -2.45 ranks 35th. The offense works because Pittsburgh's run game leads the league in rushing EPA and the defense ranks sixth. His job is to keep the chains moving underneath and not lose the game. The 6.88 intended air yards fits a career trend: his aDOT has slid from 9.2 in 2016 to 6.0 last year. This is who he is now, not a slump.

Where he still works is the short and middle of the field. On throws of 0-9 air yards he is completing 72.1% at +4.5 CPOE with 9 of his 13 touchdowns. Throws between the numbers return 0.518 EPA per attempt, by far his best direction. The intermediate band (0.307 EPA on 48 attempts) still pays when he takes it. The tight ends are the only targets returning positive value: Freiermuth (0.228 per target) and Washington (0.297). DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Jaylen Warren all sit slightly below zero.

The numbers hide where the losses come from. Deep balls are a coin flip at best: 18.9% completions, -16.6 CPOE, 3 TDs and 3 INTs. Screens and throws behind the line are bleeding value (-13.7 EPA total). Third down is the real problem: -0.363 EPA per play, a 30.4% conversion rate, and 15 of his 23 sacks. His 37.1% pressure-to-sack rate ranks 34th of 42. He scrambles on just 1.3% of dropbacks, so pressure ends plays instead of extending them. That mark has crept up for years (.315 in 2024, .341 in 2025), which points to a statue in the pocket, not a protection fluke. The line isn't the excuse: he is pressured on only 19.9% of dropbacks, a middle-of-the-pack rate.

The trend is not his friend. Over the last three games the team is 3-0, but he is at -0.138 EPA per dropback with a 2.9% TD rate and 212.3 yards a game. The Week 8 line was 13 of 25 at -11 CPOE. Even so, McCarthy keeps him busy: 36 attempts a game and a pass rate over expected ranked fifth. That keeps the yardage (233.9 a game, 16th) respectable even as the efficiency erodes.

strengths.title: Short-area accuracy and timing
strengths.body: Inside 10 air yards he's still precise: 72.1% completions at +4.5 CPOE on 0-9 yard throws, with nine touchdowns. It's anticipation and footwork rather than arm, which is why it has aged better than his deep ball. It should hold, because it's the core of the scheme.

strengths.title: Middle of the field, tight ends
strengths.body: Throws between the numbers return 0.518 EPA per attempt, and the two tight ends are his most efficient targets. Freiermuth and Washington work the seams and the zone voids underneath. They also give him reads he can hit on time, before pressure arrives.

strengths.title: Elite run game cover
strengths.body: Pittsburgh ranks first in rushing EPA, which keeps him in manageable downs and under center. He's actually positive there (0.046 EPA, versus -0.143 in shotgun). As long as the ground game holds, he doesn't have to carry the offense.

concerns.title: Third down collapses
concerns.body: On third down he's at -0.363 EPA per play with a 30.4% conversion rate, and 15 of his 23 sacks came there. Long-yardage downs (7.5 to go on average) take away the quick game and force him to hold the ball. He can't escape when that happens. It's structural: obvious passing downs expose his lack of mobility and fading arm.

concerns.title: The deep ball is gone
concerns.body: On throws of 20+ air yards he completes 18.9% at -16.6 CPOE, with as many interceptions as touchdowns. His career aDOT has fallen steadily, and last season's 6.0 says this is age, not variance. Expect the shot plays to stay rare and mostly empty.

concerns.title: Efficiency sliding lately
concerns.body: The last three games are worse than his season in EPA per dropback, yards per attempt and TD rate, despite a 3-0 record. Completion percentage is down 4.9 points from last season, and interceptions per game are up. The volume is masking a passer playing at the bottom third of the league.

trend.note: His best stretch was Weeks 3-5, including +8.5 EPA against Cincinnati. Since then he has strung together a -13.5 game against Tampa's top-two defense, a small positive at New Orleans, and a 13-of-25 dud against Cleveland, all while the team kept winning.

nextGame.headline: Bengals' soft underneath defense fits him; their offense dictates volume.
nextGame.body:
Cincinnati is the rare defense built to let him do what he does well. It ranks 25th against short passes but fourth against deep ones. That rewards the 0-9 yard game and costs little for the shots he rarely hits anyway. Tight ends have feasted: TE1s score 4.3 PPR above their averages against the Bengals (30th), and tight ends draw an above-league share of targets. Quarterbacks have piled up 279.4 yards a game on them, 30th. On the other side sits the league's second-best offense, which also leads the league in passing over expectation. A 48.5 total with Pittsburgh as a 3.5-point underdog points to a game where he has to keep throwing. That suits his volume, even if his best game this year (292 yards, 3 TDs against this team in Week 3) set a high bar.

Availability is mostly neutral. Michael Pittman Jr. carries an estimated return date of this game, but he said he has no clear timeline to come off injured reserve, so don't count on a new outside option. Cincinnati lost edge rusher Cashius Howell to IR, which thins a pass rush that ranks ninth in sack rate. Pittsburgh comes off a bye with 14 days of rest.

keyMatchups.title: Tight ends vs Bengals coverage
keyMatchups.body: Freiermuth and Washington are his only positive-EPA targets, and Cincinnati allows tight ends 4.3 PPR over their averages, near the bottom of the league. This is the cleanest edge on the board. Expect heavy seam and middle-of-field work.

keyMatchups.title: Short game vs soft underneath
keyMatchups.body: Cincinnati's short-pass defense ranks 25th, right where Rodgers lives. Its deep defense ranks fourth, so forced shots will likely die. Efficiency hinges on staying patient underneath.

keyMatchups.title: Shootout script vs run game
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh's first-ranked rush offense meets a run defense ranked 27th, which argues for ball control. But the Bengals' passing offense ranks second. If Pittsburgh falls behind, he becomes a trailing passer, where he has been at -0.214 EPA per play.

nextGame.watch: Third-and-long against the Bengals' rush. If Pittsburgh's run game keeps him in short yardage, he can pick this defense apart. If it doesn't, the sacks pile up.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect more of the same shape: steady volume in a pass-leaning scheme, short and middle efficiency, and value bleeding out on third downs, screens and deep shots. The yardage is sustainable because the attempts are. The 4.5% TD rate is near league average and has held up mostly through short red-zone throws, but the last three games already show it slipping. His red-zone efficiency (-0.238 EPA) suggests some regression downward. The pressure-to-sack habit has worsened for three straight seasons and won't fix itself at 43.

The ceiling rests on the run game and defense keeping games close and manageable. A projection around 215-245 yards and 1.2-1.7 touchdowns a game fits. Expect roughly an interception every other game and close to three sacks a week. Shootouts like this Cincinnati game push the yardage up. Tight, run-heavy wins against division defenses pull it toward the low end.
swingFactors: Whether the top-ranked run game keeps him out of third-and-long
Pittman's return adding a reliable outside target
Game scripts that force him to throw from behind

confidence.note: Eight starts is a modest sample, but the decline lines up with a multi-year career trend.
